newsitem.title: CHILE: Andina sees Brazilian business recovering.
newsitem.headline: Andina sees Brazilian business recovering.

text.p: Embotelladora Andina's Brazilian unit expects a stronger 1997 after flat soft drink sales in the first nine months of this year, executives at the Chilean bottler said.

Soft drink and beer volumes rose 11 percent in October over the same month last year at Andina's Rio de Janeiro Refrescos after an "adverse stage" during the rest of the year, they said in a conference call.
Andina's Chilean and Argentine operations were both doing well, with soft drink sales volumes expected to rise 8-9 percent in Chile next year and 14-16 INTERRUPTED
Rio de Janeiro Refrescos sales by volume fell 1.7 percent in the first nine months of the year over the same period last year and down 8.9 percent in the third quarter.

They attributed the drop to slacking purchases of consumer goods in general in Brazil this year and unusually cool weather. But Olivos added Andina would "work on Rio de Janeiro Refrescos' efficiency to reach the growth margins we expect for the future."
Andina expects stronger demand, not through price discounts, plus productivity increases next year at Rio de Janeiro Refrescos, which the Chilean company bought in 1994.

It expected soft drink volume to rise 7-8 percent and its beer sales volume to rise 50 percent, they said. Andina's market share in all three markets -- Argentina, Chile and Brazil -- was expected to rise one to two percent next year, said Chief Operations Officer Luis Rivera.
In Argentina, where Andina owns 95 percent of Embotelladoras del Atlantico SA, sales volume rose 24 percent in the first nine months of the year to 7.5 million unit cases, officials said.

Andina reported a consolidated net profit of 23.7 billion pesos in the first nine months of this year, on revenues of 95.70 billion, compared with 19.8 billion in the first nine months of last year on revenues of 88.66 billion pesos.
